Applied the S34 request: the shadow paragraph now states N28b-38's selector exactly (durable per-node ordinal n, phase p from BLAKE3(kind ‖ version ‖ key), shadow when (n + p) mod 64 = 0; the key fixes the phase, the ordinal the rate), so each class's shared node is shadowed once in every 64 of its member hits. Acceptance and `shadow_selection_one_in_64` followed it: detection is certain within 64 hits of one node and bounded by (63/64)^640 ≈ 4·10⁻⁵ over 640 hits on distinct nodes (recomputed); repeated member hits give exactly 100 of 6,400, not a binomial band.

ADR-GAUNT-01 says frob-conformance is 'library plus test targets; no binary, no verb', and the lint no_conformance_command scans only `frob conformance` and `frob-conformance record`. 37 beads' scripts invoke `frob-conformance run <check> …` as if it were a binary, so they pass the lint and fail at run time: BD-350, N28c-03, -05, -06, -08, -09, -11, -13, -14, -15, -16, -17, -18, -19, -26, -27, -28, -31, -32, -34, -35, -36, -37, -39, -40, -41, N30a-26, -39, -44, -48, N30b-24, -30, -32, -34, -35 (N28c-42 and N28c-43, in S43, are converted to `cargo run -p <owning crate> --example <name> -- …`). Add `frob-conformance run` (any invocation of a frob-conformance binary) to the lint's literals and state the two admitted replacements (a cargo test target with FROB_TEST_SEED for a Gauntlet row; an `--example` of the owning crate for a harness reader or driver), so the owners of those beads can convert them.
